prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1272; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for low-speed head-on collision. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed into the lane during a slight curve. Both drivers stopped at scene, no police response required. Claimant reports wrist pain and has since retained counsel, who has requested all future contact be directed to their office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and obtain the medical authorization. Attorney advised that the claimant was evaluated at urgent care and diagnosed with a wrist fracture. Requested copies of all treatment records and itemized bills. Advised that liability is under review and no offer will be made until records are received.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos from both vehicles. Damage is consistent with a low-speed frontal impact, with bumper cover and hood contact on both sides. Scheduled independent appraisal for the claimant's vehicle. Noted that the insured's dashcam footage was reviewed and shows the other vehicle drifting left before contact.

Entry 4: Received the orthopedic consult notes from the claimant's treating physician through counsel. Records confirm a closed fracture of the distal radius, treated with a splint and referral to a hand specialist. Recovery timeline is listed as ongoing. Placed the file on medical review and requested a records summary from our nurse reviewer.

Entry 5: Nurse reviewer summary received. Findings support the reported injury as consistent with the collision mechanism. Liability assessment completed, with the other driver assigned majority fault. Sent a written status update to claimant's counsel and set a diary to follow up on outstanding specialist records in two weeks.
